newsitem.title: FRANCE: Estonian premier pledges progress on refugees.
newsitem.headline: Estonian premier pledges progress on refugees.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vahi pledged before the Council of Europe on Monday to improve the plight of refugees in his country.

"Tomorrow, my government will submit to parliament the Geneva convention on refugees and the right to asylum," Vahi told the Council's parliamentary assembly. He said later a vote could take place next month.
The 40-member council aims to protect human rights and democracy.
In answer to a question from a Russian deputy, the premier said that all foreigners -- chiefly Russians -- who own a temporary residence permit would be given a permanent permit this year.

A report by the Council of Europe concluded that Estonia has made progress on several of the human rights commitments it made when it joined the Council in 1993, but that progress was still needed in four areas.

The report highlighted internment of refugees and asylum-seekers, the granting of Estonian nationality to a Russian-speaking minority, capital punishment which is still in force, and conditions for preventive detention which it deemed "deplorable".
